title: Family
author: Bradley, Anthony B.
summary: Anthony Bradley's essay examines a pivotal contrast between documented cases of bystanders who filmed tragedies passively and a July 2024 incident in Butler, Pennsylvania, where bystanders instead put down their phones and ran toward danger. Bradley uses this contrast as a lens for examining a deeper question about character formation in the smartphone age: whether the reflexive reach for a device during crisis is eroding the instinct for courageous civic action. The essay draws on virtue ethics to argue that habituation matters, since what we practice in low-stakes moments shapes what we do in high-stakes moments. Bradley locates the difference not in character type but in what those individuals had habituated their attention and hands to do over time. The essay is a call for deliberate counter-formation: for parents, schools, and communities to cultivate the reflex of action alongside the discipline of observation.
points: The reflexive reach for a phone during crisis, to document rather than intervene, represents not cowardice but a habituated default that smartphone culture has spent a decade training into human behavior.

Virtue ethics predicts that patterns practiced in ordinary circumstances become the instinctive responses exhibited in extraordinary ones: what we do with our hands and attention every day shapes what we do in a crisis.

The Butler incident demonstrates that the phone-first default is not universal and can be interrupted by prior character formation: individuals who instinctively ran toward danger had cultivated different habits of response.

Bradley's diagnosis is institutional as much as personal: if schools, families, and communities reward and celebrate documentation over action, they are habituating the next generation toward passive witnessing.

Counter-formation requires more than discouraging phone use; it requires deliberately practicing courage, intervention, and civic responsibility in low-stakes contexts so those capacities are available when the stakes are high.
